model_card.name: champion
model_card.fairness_note: Fairness audited on the holdout by zip_code (notebook 04, section 7): the policy tree would email Urban customers at 59% against their 41% population share — a zip-proxy contact disparity, flagged here rather than smoothed over. Group uplift intervals all exclude zero and overlap each other: no group-level effect disparity is supported, but group-level causal claims are not the model's to make either.
when_not_to_use: Not validated outside the Hillstrom email experiment — no claim transfers to another audience, channel or period.
Do not target on predicted *spend*: the spend ordering sat inside its own random noise floor (Day 3, notebook 03 section 6).
Do not present the champion's edge over the DR-learner as a win: its 10-seed Qini edge (0.0048) is inside its own spread — a statistical tie, broken on profit and parsimony only.
Not for individual-level causal claims ("this customer will convert because of the email") — intervals are wide per customer.
Do not use visit-scores as conversion-probabilities without the per-arm recalibration from notebook 03 (raw Brier skill vs base rate is ~zero).
limitations: Trained on the mens-email arm only; the womens arm is a separate fit.
Randomized-experiment features (7 covariates) — richer behavioural data would likely move the ranking more than any learner swap has.
Single-seed artifact; the honest performance envelope is the 10-seed benchmark in docs/concepts.md, not this file's one-shot metrics.

copilot_demos.question: I have $500 to spend on contacts at $0.10 each — how deep should I target and what should I expect to earn?
copilot_demos.note: full plan request with both budget and contact cost stated
copilot_demos.prose:
## Recommendation
Target the top 50% of the ranked customer list (4,262 contacts at $0.10 each). The sweep does not clear its own contact cost until 2%, so do not widen the list beyond that on this evidence.
## What it earns
The champion ranking is estimated to deliver 33.87 incremental conversions (standard error 13.33) and a profit of $756.32 (95% interval [-$155.64, $1,668.27]).
## Uncertainties
The interval above is a normal approximation on one holdout; when it spans zero the honest read is a range, not a promise. The depth sweep only breaks even from 2%, and its point-estimate optimum (28.7%, $946.50) is a single-split estimate, not a measurement.
## Assumptions
- value per conversion and cost per contact come from configs/business_assumptions.yaml (fixed, not estimated per request)
## Next test
Confirm on live traffic before scaling: at a +1 percentage-point MDE on the visit rate, plan for 15,499 customers per arm (30,998 total, 16 days at 2,000 eligible per day).

Model: champion (response on visit).

copilot_demos.question: Plan a $2,000 email campaign for me — who should get it?
copilot_demos.note: budget-only plan request; cost per contact comes from the default
copilot_demos.prose:
## Recommendation
Prioritise the 3 segment(s) the policy tree labels for email (segment 2, segment 3, segment 5) and hold back the 3 labelled no-email.
## Segments
- Segment 0 (onehot__zip_code_Urban <= 0.5, num__history <= 468.4, num__history <= 100.4): 21.7% of the holdout (1,851 customers); policy says **no email**; measured visit uplift +0.0675 (95% interval [+0.0369, +0.0981]).
- Segment 1 (onehot__zip_code_Urban <= 0.5, num__history <= 468.4, num__history > 100.4): 29.1% of the holdout (2,480 customers); policy says **no email**; measured visit uplift +0.0854 (95% interval [+0.0569, +0.1139]).
- Segment 2 (onehot__zip_code_Urban <= 0.5, num__history > 468.4): 8.5% of the holdout (720 customers); policy says **email**; measured visit uplift +0.1024 (95% interval [+0.0471, +0.1576]).
- Segment 3 (onehot__zip_code_Urban > 0.5, num__history <= 475, onehot__channel_Phone <= 0.5): 18.8% of the holdout (1,605 customers); policy says **email**; measured visit uplift +0.0530 (95% interval [+0.0184, +0.0877]).
- Segment 4 (onehot__zip_code_Urban > 0.5, num__history <= 475, onehot__channel_Phone > 0.5): 16.5% of the holdout (1,409 customers); policy says **no email**; measured visit uplift +0.0848 (95% interval [+0.0513, +0.1184]).
- Segment 5 (onehot__zip_code_Urban > 0.5, num__history > 475): 5.4% of the holdout (458 customers); policy says **email**; measured visit uplift +0.0870 (95% interval [+0.0232, +0.1507]).
The strongest email-labelled segment is segment 2 at +0.1024 on visits.
## Uncertainties
Rules come from an honest DRPolicyTree capped at max_depth; every uplift number is re-measured on the untouched holdout as treated-minus-control within the segment, with a 95% normal-approximation interval. Small segments are noisy by construction — read the interval before the point.
- Rural: contacted at 13.7% (1,288 customers), uplift +0.0829 (95% interval [+0.0399, +0.1259]). 
- Suburban: contacted at 14.4% (3,763 customers), uplift +0.0785 (95% interval [+0.0568, +0.1002]). 
- Urban: contacted at 59.4% (3,472 customers), uplift +0.0709 (95% interval [+0.0482, +0.0935]). 
## Assumptions
- value per conversion and cost per contact come from configs/business_assumptions.yaml (fixed, not estimated per request)

copilot_demos.question: How long should we test a new offer? We see 2,000 customers a day.
copilot_demos.note: daily volume stated; MDE defaults and must be flagged
copilot_demos.prose:
## Recommendation
Run the confirmatory test for 16 days: 15,499 customers per arm (30,998 total) at 2,000 eligible per day, splitting traffic evenly between email and no-email.
## What to watch
Primary metric: visit rate, baseline 0.1061 in control. Detect an absolute lift of 1 percentage points (9.43% relative) at alpha 0.05 and power 0.8; call it success only if the confidence interval excludes zero.
## Uncertainties
This sizing uses the classic two-proportion normal approximation with the baseline treated as known, so keep headroom; the baseline itself is estimated from one holdout.
## Assumptions
- value per conversion and cost per contact come from configs/business_assumptions.yaml (fixed, not estimated per request)
- MDE defaulted to +1 percentage points on the visit rate

The champion ranking is estimated to deliver 31.89 incremental conversions (standard error 10.49) and a profit of $857.60 (95% interval [$139.55, $1,575.65]).
## Uncertainties
The interval above is a normal approximation on one holdout; when it spans zero the honest read is a range, not a promise. The depth sweep only breaks even from 2%, and its point-estimate optimum (28.7%, $946.50) is a single-split estimate, not a measurement.
## Assumptions
- value per conversion and cost per contact come from configs/business_assumptions.yaml (fixed, not estimated per request)
- cost per contact defaulted to $0.10 (configs/business_assumptions.yaml)
- targeting depth defaulted to 30% (no budget stated)
## Next test
Confirm on live traffic before scaling: at a +1 percentage-point MDE on the visit rate, plan for 15,499 customers per arm (30,998 total, 16 days at 2,000 eligible per day).

output.note: Profit valued on the money outcome (conversions), treated-minus-control within the targeted set; 95% intervals are normal-approximation and widen sharply at shallow depths. Two-proportion normal approximation, two-sided alpha, equal allocation; baseline treated as known. Duration assumes the daily eligible pool is split evenly between arms.

output.fairness_note: Fairness audited on the holdout by zip_code (notebook 04, section 7): the policy tree would email Urban customers at 59% against their 41% population share — a zip-proxy contact disparity, flagged here rather than smoothed over. Group uplift intervals all exclude zero and overlap each other: no group-level effect disparity is supported, but group-level causal claims are not the model's to make either.
when_not_to_use: Not validated outside the Hillstrom email experiment — no claim transfers to another audience, channel or period.
Do not target on predicted *spend*: the spend ordering sat inside its own random noise floor (Day 3, notebook 03 section 6).
Do not present the champion's edge over the DR-learner as a win: its 10-seed Qini edge (0.0048) is inside its own spread — a statistical tie, broken on profit and parsimony only.
Not for individual-level causal claims ("this customer will convert because of the email") — intervals are wide per customer.
Do not use visit-scores as conversion-probabilities without the per-arm recalibration from notebook 03 (raw Brier skill vs base rate is ~zero).
limitations: Trained on the mens-email arm only; the womens arm is a separate fit.
Randomized-experiment features (7 covariates) — richer behavioural data would likely move the ranking more than any learner swap has.
Single-seed artifact; the honest performance envelope is the 10-seed benchmark in docs/concepts.md, not this file's one-shot metrics.
